stem: Which growth pattern is most consistent with healthy infant growth?

options.text: Serial measurements that track along percentiles with weight and length in proportion
A single weight above the 97th percentile regardless of proportionality
Any infant whose weight is below the 50th percentile
Crossing down percentile lines despite preserved appetite
Weight gain without considering length or height

explanation: Serial measurements that track along percentiles with weight and length in proportion is the correct answer. Healthy growth is judged by the pattern over time and proportionality, rather than by one isolated measurement.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because healthy growth is shown by serial measurements that follow a consistent percentile pattern, with weight and length remaining proportionate.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a single high weight measurement does not by itself indicate healthy growth and does not assess proportionality over time.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because weight below the 50th percentile can still be normal if the child is growing consistently and proportionately.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because crossing down percentile lines suggests faltering growth rather than a healthy pattern.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because growth assessment must include length or height as well as weight, with attention to proportionality.
